business_snapshot.title: Business snapshot
business_snapshot.content: TCS provides IT services, consulting, and business solutions to major enterprises to support their transformational journeys through a comprehensive portfolio spanning application development, digital transformation, AI, data and cloud services, and cybersecurity [3, 4]. The company organizes its business segments by industry verticals, which comprise Banking, Financial Services and Insurance, Manufacturing, Consumer Business, Communication, Media and Technology, Life Sciences and Healthcare, and Others [1]. Its revenue mix is led by Banking, Financial Services and Insurance at 38.7%, followed by Consumer Business (15.9%), Communication, Media and Technology (14.8%), Life Sciences and Healthcare (10.4%), Manufacturing (10.2%), and Others at 10.0% [8].

trajectory.title: Trajectory
trajectory.content: Over the past five financial years, TCS achieved a compound annual growth rate in revenue of 10.2%, demonstrating the resilience and scalability of its business model [1]. Concurrently, the company steadily increased its Earnings Per Share, recording a compound annual growth rate of 10.3% over the same five-year period [6]. Operating margins expanded to 25% in FY 2026, reaching a four-year high driven by improvements in business mix, productivity, realisation, pyramid rebalancing, and favourable currency movements [6].

balance_sheet.title: Balance sheet
balance_sheet.content: The company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.1 times, where debt consists of borrowings and lease liabilities [1]. The debt service coverage ratio stands at a healthy 19.8 times [1]. Regarding working capital, the current ratio is reported at 2.0 times, down slightly from 2.1 times in the previous year [1]. Additionally, the net capital turnover ratio is 4.0 times based on revenue from operations and average working capital [2].

cash_quality.title: Cash quality
cash_quality.content: TCS has demonstrated a strong cash conversion ratio, reflecting effective generation of operational cash and a solid financial position [2]. The company's cash conversion remained strong at 93% of net income [6]. Furthermore, TCS remains committed to returning substantial free cash flows to its shareholders while judiciously investing to support long-term growth aspirations [6].

guidance.title: Guidance
content: Management will continue investments to maximize growth while maintaining operational rigor to optimize margins, achieve robust cash conversion, and strengthen the balance sheet.
Management is prioritizing growth and expects capacity creation to reflect in revenues in the coming quarters, while looking towards inching up margins from current levels.
For the data center business, management plans to expand capacity once contracts are secured, with revenues expected to start kicking in 18 to 24 months thereafter.

bull: Operating margins for FY26 reached 25%, representing a 70 basis point expansion over the prior year and hitting a 4-year high [1].
Cash conversion remains robust, exceeding 100% of net profits with net cash from operations at $1.6 billion (106.7% of net income) in Q4 [3].
The company maintains the highest margin level in the industry, showing strong margins while the rest of the industry faces pressure [5].
bear: Full year FY26 constant currency revenue declined by 2.4% YoY (and reported dollar revenue declined by 0.5%) [3].
Operating margins exclude certain exceptional one-off items recognised during the year, such as severance-related expenses, legal provisions, and India wage code changes [1].
